meta.title: All Platforms, protein measurement catalog
meta.scope: Protein-measurement platforms only. Excludes EV/vesicle-capture chemistries, spatial/tissue imaging, non-proteomic comparators.

evaluation_levels.1_deep_score: Ten-axis Platform Comparison score (coverage, precision, specificity, sensitivity, cost, throughput, quant-type, matrix, evidence, pQTL). Reserved for platforms characterisable on ALL ten axes, the integrated tier.
evaluation_levels.2_integration_readiness: Lighter three-input readiness score (maturity + validation + tier) for platforms that are deployable AND have an independent validation basis. These are ranked here.
evaluation_levels.3_emerging_not_scored: Pre-commercial or platforms with no independent validation basis. Catalogued for awareness, but deliberately NOT scored or rank-ordered, assigning a number would imply a discrimination the evidence does not support.

meta.ranking_axis: apt_readiness_rank_v1 = round(0.5*maturity + 0.3*validation + 0.2*(4-tier_number), 0.25); readiness_precise gives the unrounded value used as tiebreak. Applied to scoreable service_assay rows only. Readiness measures integration-readiness, NOT platform quality, a deeply-characterised open-MS service (Seer, Biognosys) ranks lower here because it lacks a fixed content list, yet is Integrated via the ten-axis comparison.

tiers.T1: Fixed published per-protein content list, directly comparable
tiers.T2: Defined but narrow/custom panel, comparable per configuration
tiers.T3: No fixed analyte list (open MS / de novo), reference, not panel-comparable

meta.availability_note: availability_status verified via targeted 2026 web search for flagship/at-risk products (Olink Explore 3072 retired; SomaScan 7K superseded-but-orderable).
meta.excluded_adjacent: Autoantibody-serology arrays (Sengenics i-Ome), single-cell ADT panels (Proteintech MultiPro), and fixed clinical LDTs (PromarkerD) were considered and excluded as out-of-scope adjacent modalities.
meta.independence_gate: A non-integrated platform is scored only if its MEASUREMENT CHEMISTRY has independent (non-vendor) peer-reviewed validation. Vendor posters, press, and spec sheets do not count. Platforms failing the gate (e.g. ProteinXI, novel MSD ImmunoLock NGS chemistry, vendor AACR poster only) are catalogued as Emerging with no score/rank. Integrated platforms are exempt (already established via the ten-axis comparison). The validation_basis field records each scored row's evidence. The gate was applied catalog-wide as a DISCLOSURE standard, not only an exclusion rule: the six APT-assessed platforms are exempt from exclusion because they clear inclusion on structural grounds (commercially deployable, T1 content-list-anchored, characterisable on all ten axes) and carry full ten-axis scores, but where an integrated platform's headline figure is vendor-stated (notably Nomic Omni 1000's ~1,000-plex coverage, independently validated only at ~191-plex) this is disclosed and is already reflected in a low evidence_depth score and is not silently exempted.
meta.verification: Ranked rows independently re-derived blind (verifiers saw only name+vendor) and diffed against the catalog. Per-cell grade in verification_matrix.csv: 10 green (peer-reviewed, high-confidence), 15 amber (chemistry independently validated but a product-specific figure vendor-stated), 0 red (no fabricated/unsourced citations). Corrections applied: 4 maturity downgrades (shipping≠established), Nautilus T3→T2 (shipping product is defined Tau panel), Portal maturity→0 + citation fixed to Sauciuc Nat Biotechnol 2023.
meta.score_status_note: score_status: 'APT-assessed' = the integrated set scored on all ten axes; 'preliminary' = readiness-only score for platforms not yet in the deep comparison; '' = emerging/enabling (no score).
meta.overview_note: Plain-English 'About' overviews are generated from the catalog's own verified fields (chemistry, plex, matrix, quantitation, validation) plus textbook-level explanation of each assay class. No platform-specific number, date, or citation appears that is not in the verified record.

overview.about: Olink Explore HT is a proteomics service assay that measures over 5,400 human proteins simultaneously from a few microliters of plasma, serum, or CSF. It uses Proximity Extension Assay technology: pairs of antibodies coupled to DNA oligonucleotides bind a target protein, whose DNA oligonucleotides then hybridize and are extended by a DNA polymerase to extension into a reporter sequence. These reporters are sequenced on Illumina or Ultima platforms, generating protein abundance measurements. The platform delivers relative quantitation across thousands of proteins in a single run, enabling broad unbiased surveys of the plasma proteome.
overview.best_for: Large-scale exploratory studies seeking broad plasma protein signatures across many samples.
strengths: Multiplexes 5,400+ proteins in one assay, reducing sample volume burden.
Achieves sub-femtomolar sensitivity with CVs below 5% for well-detected proteins.
Processes up to 344 samples per run at established service providers.
limitations: Relative quantitation only; cannot anchor to absolute protein copy numbers.
Low median cross-platform correlation (0.14) with other large-plex panels suggests platform-specific bias.
Requires NGS infrastructure and bioinformatic processing, extending turnaround time.

overview.about: SomaScan 11K is a fixed-panel proteomics platform that measures approximately 9,900 unique proteins in plasma, serum, CSF, and other biofluids using modified DNA aptamers (SOMAmer reagents). Each aptamer is a short DNA strand that binds to a specific protein target; the platform hybridizes these aptamers to a microarray and quantifies binding via fluorescent readout. The 11K panel offers broad protein coverage in a single assay with high throughput in a clinical laboratory setting, trading the flexibility of mass spectrometry for standardized, reproducible measurements across thousands of proteins simultaneously.
overview.best_for: Large cohort studies requiring consistent, reproducible measurement of ~9,900 proteins across hundreds of samples.
strengths: Simultaneously quantifies ~9,900 proteins from a single 55 microliter sample
Median CV ~5% (vendor tech note) with high reproducibility (split-sample r=0.85)
Available as CLIA/CAP certified service with hundreds-per-week throughput
limitations: Relative quantitation only (RFU); no absolute protein concentration
Binds one epitope per protein; cannot distinguish proteoforms or PTM variants
High cost per sample; fixed panel limits discovery of unmeasured proteins

overview.about: SomaScan 7K is a multiplexed protein measurement platform that quantifies approximately 7,000 protein targets from small-volume plasma, serum, cerebrospinal fluid, or urine samples. The platform uses SOMAmer aptamers, short DNA sequences engineered to bind specific proteins with high specificity, captured on a microarray and read via fluorescence. Each sample produces relative quantitation (RFU values) across all targets in parallel. The 7K version measures roughly 6,400 unique proteins and has been retired in favor of the 11K platform, though analytical validation showed comparable median coefficient of variation between the two versions.
overview.best_for: Large cohort studies requiring broad protein profiling across plasma, serum, or CSF samples.
strengths: Measures ~7,000 protein targets from 55 µL sample volume
Validated across multiple biological matrices including CSF
High-throughput capacity of hundreds of samples per week
limitations: Provides relative quantitation only (RFU), not absolute protein amounts
Platform retired; no longer commercially available
No proteoform or post-translational modification resolution

overview.about: The Olink Explore 3072 is a retired multiplex protein measurement platform that quantifies a large fixed panel of proteins in blood and cerebrospinal fluid using dual-antibody proximity extension assay (PEA) chemistry. PEA works by pairing antibodies that bind a target protein; when brought close together, they extend DNA strands that are then amplified and counted by next-generation sequencing, yielding relative abundance measurements. Its distinctive feature is a large fixed panel enabling broad proteomic surveys from minimal sample volume. Quantitation is relative, not absolute.
overview.best_for: Large-scale genetic association studies and biobank cohorts requiring broad protein coverage.
strengths: Large fixed panel of ~3,000 assays from minimal sample input
Strong cis-pQTL support: 72% of assays validated in UK Biobank
High throughput capacity of approximately 1,000 samples per week
limitations: Retired platform with no ongoing support or new assay development
Relative quantitation only; cannot measure absolute protein amounts
CSF measurements show weak correlation with mass spectrometry effect sizes

overview.about: The Alamar NULISAseq Neuro 220 Panel measures 220 proteins from the central nervous system and neurology using a nucleic-acid-linked immunosandwich assay. Each target protein is captured by antibodies, then tagged with short DNA barcodes and released into solution. These DNA barcodes are amplified and sequenced on an automated high-throughput instrument, generating counts proportional to protein abundance. The platform accepts minimal sample volume (10 microliters), works across multiple matrices including cerebrospinal fluid and blood, and includes discrete phosphorylated tau variants relevant to neurodegeneration. It provides relative quantitation with reported single-digit attomolar sensitivity.
overview.best_for: Biomarker discovery and validation studies in neurodegeneration and CNS disease cohorts.
strengths: Measures 220 CNS targets including phospho-tau epitopes in 10 µL sample
Validated performance across plasma, CSF, and alternative matrices (EVs, tears, microsampling)
Median CVs ~5–6% in plasma, ~9% in CSF; high correlation with reference methods
limitations: Relative quantitation only; no absolute concentration values
Limited to discrete phospho-epitopes; no untargeted PTM discovery
Detectability in CSF ~85% of targets versus ~95% in plasma

overview.about: Targeted MRM/PRM panels measure 10–100 proteins in a single sample using mass spectrometry. The assay works by converting proteins to peptides, then using a mass spectrometer to detect specific peptide fragments while comparing them to isotope-labeled standards, a quantitative reference that mirrors the target peptide exactly. This approach yields absolute protein concentrations (not just relative ranks) with tight reproducibility. The platform is distinctive for handling protein variants and post-translational modifications at predefined sites, and for working across diverse sample types including cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, and urine, useful for biomarker validation and clinical translation.
strengths: Absolute quantitation with <10–15% coefficients of variation
Detects protein variants and post-translational modifications at specified sites
Works in multiple matrices including CSF, plasma, serum, and urine
limitations: Requires method development and optimization before deployment
Limited to pre-specified targets; no discovery of unexpected proteins
Sample volumes and throughput constrained by LC-MS instrument time
overview.best_for: Biomarker validation and clinical translation studies requiring absolute quantitation.

overview.about: Olink Target 48/96 and Flex are targeted protein panels measuring defined sets of 45-92 proteins (or up to ~30 custom markers with Flex) in plasma, serum, CSF, dried blood spots, or extracellular vesicle preparations, using just 1 microliter of sample. The core method, proximity extension assay (PEA), pairs two antibodies per target, each tagged with a short DNA strand; when both bind the same protein, the strands hybridize and are extended by a polymerase, generating a new DNA sequence quantified by real-time PCR. Because detection requires both antibodies binding simultaneously, background cross-reactivity is reduced. Target 48 yields absolute concentrations (pg/mL) via calibrators, while Target 96 gives relative NPX units. Panels have supported large CSF biomarker discovery work in Parkinson's disease.
strengths: Absolute pg/mL quantitation available via Target 48 calibrators
Minimal sample volume required, just 1 microliter
Used in large peer-reviewed CSF Parkinson's discovery cohorts
limitations: Targeted panel limited to under 100 proteins
No proteoform or PTM resolution
Target 96 reports relative NPX, not absolute concentration
overview.best_for: Best suited for hypothesis-driven biomarker studies needing precise, low-volume quantitation of a defined protein set.

overview.about: Quanterix Simoa is a targeted immunoassay platform that measures specific proteins and protein modifications in serum, plasma, and cerebrospinal fluid. It uses single-molecule digital ELISA: magnetic beads coated with capture antibodies are distributed into femtolitre wells, where each bead-bound protein is detected and counted individually.Absolute quantitation still uses a calibrator/standard curve; the single-molecule digital regime improves sensitivity and precision at very low concentrations. The platform is configured for 1–6 analytes per run, with specialized assays for neurological biomarkers like phosphorylated tau variants and alpha-synuclein. It delivers absolute quantitation across validated matrices.
overview.best_for: Biomarker studies in neurodegenerative disease requiring multi-site CSF and plasma sampling.
strengths: Measures phospho-epitopes (p-tau181/217/231, pS129-alpha-synuclein) with clinical validation
CSF-validated with specified limits of detection; serum/plasma compatibility
Digital single-molecule detection avoids standard-curve artifacts
limitations: Low throughput (66–96 samples per run) relative to high-plex platforms
Targeted assays only; no discovery of novel biomarkers
CSF detection limits 100-fold higher than plasma for same biomarkers

overview.about: Luminex xMAP/INTELLIFLEX is a bead-based sandwich immunoassay platform that measures absolute concentrations of a defined panel of proteins in serum, plasma, CSF, or culture supernatant. Each protein target is captured by antibody-coated polystyrene microspheres carrying a unique internal spectral barcode; a flow-based reader identifies each bead's color code and measures a fluorescent reporter antibody bound in the sandwich, converting signal to pg/mL via standard curves, similar in principle to ELISA but run on many bead colors simultaneously. Practical panels run 10-50 analytes, well below the bead system's spectral ceiling, because antibody cross-reactivity limits true multiplexing. It is a mature, low-cost, high-throughput workhorse, though sensitivity for low-abundance CNS analytes trails newer digital immunoassay platforms.
strengths: Low cost with fast 96-well throughput (~20 min)
Absolute quantitation in pg/mL via standard curves
Long-standing validated use across serum, plasma, CSF
limitations: Lower sensitivity than digital ELISA for low-abundance cytokines
Practical multiplexing well below spectral bead ceiling
No proteoform or PTM resolution
overview.best_for: Routine, cost-sensitive targeted cytokine or biomarker panels needing absolute concentrations at moderate multiplexing.

overview.about: Ella is an automated immunoassay platform that measures the absolute concentration of specific proteins in liquid samples like serum, plasma, or cell lysate. It works using a sandwich immunoassay: capture antibodies bind a target protein, and a second labeled antibody binds it from another side, producing a signal proportional to how much protein is present. Ella automates this process inside a microfluidic cartridge containing tiny glass nanoreactors, which run each sample in built-in triplicate and keep different target antibodies in separate channels to avoid cross-reactivity. Results are read against factory-calibrated standard curves, giving absolute concentrations in under 90 minutes from very small sample volumes.
strengths: Absolute quantitation in pg/mL with sub-pg/mL sensitivity
Fast turnaround, under 90 minutes per run
Minimal sample volume with built-in triplicate measurement
limitations: Low multiplexing, up to 8 analytes per cartridge
Fewer targets per run than high-plex discovery platforms
Targets fixed to validated menu or custom cartridge design
overview.best_for: Targeted, high-confidence quantification of a small protein panel across many samples, such as biomarker verification studies.

overview.about: MRM Proteomics PeptiQuant Plus delivers absolute quantitation of 125 or 270 human plasma proteins via targeted mass spectrometry. The method isolates and measures specific peptides derived from your proteins of interest using LC-MS/MS on a triple-quadrupole instrument. Each target peptide is paired with a heavy stable-isotope-labeled internal standard, allowing direct quantitation traceable to calibrated standards. Unlike discovery proteomics, this platform measures a defined protein list with high accuracy and reproducibility, following CPTAC Tier II standards for accuracy and traceability.

Fixed 125- or 270-protein panels enable direct comparisons
Available as turnkey kit or managed CRO service
limitations: Restricted to pre-defined protein list; no discovery of unexpected targets
Requires triple-quadrupole MS; not available on all labs' instruments
Plasma-optimized; extension to other matrices requires separate assay development
overview.best_for: Biomarker validation studies and clinical trials requiring absolute quantitation of predefined protein panels.

overview.about: CellCarta/Caprion offers targeted mass spectrometry biomarker quantitation using MRM and PRM on triple-quad instruments. The platform measures defined protein panels by fragmenting peptides from the target proteins and detecting specific fragment ions, enabling multiplexed relative quantitation across hundreds of proteins or precise absolute quantitation of single targets using synthetic standards. Antibody-enrichment immuno-MRM panels expand sensitivity for low-abundance biomarkers. The service supports multiple matrices and offers regulated validation pathways (GCLP/CAP-CLIA) for clinical trial use.
overview.best_for: Clinical trial biomarker verification and regulated multiplex protein screening in diverse biological matrices.
strengths: Multiplexed measurement of custom protein panels up to ~350 targets
Absolute quantitation with SIS standards for clinical-grade precision
Multi-matrix flexibility and regulated validation for trials
limitations: Requires a priori target selection; not discovery-first
Panel expansion demands assay development and revalidation

overview.about: Biognosys TrueSignature is a targeted mass spectrometry service that measures from single proteins up to several hundred (vendor-stated up to ~800) per custom panel in absolute quantities (fmol/µL). overview.about: The ProteinXI Human Discovery 400 Panel is a service assay measuring about 400 proteins in human plasma. overview.about: Encodia ProteoCode was a protein sequencing platform that aimed to read peptides one amino acid at a time and convert that information into DNA, so it could be read out on standard next-generation DNA sequencers. In principle, the peptide is degraded from its end residue by residue; each time a residue is exposed, a recognizer molecule matches it and attaches a DNA barcode encoding that amino acid's identity. Stringing these barcodes together creates a DNA 'record' of the peptide's sequence, which sequencing then decodes at high throughput. What made this platform distinctive was its 'reverse translation' concept, converting protein sequence into DNA for readout, developed by Illumina/454 veterans. The company shut down in November 2025 without ever launching a commercial product.

overview.about: The SCIEX ZenoTOF 8600 is a high-throughput mass spectrometry platform that identifies and quantifies proteins from small cell samples. overview.about: Thermo Scientific Stellar MS is a targeted mass spectrometry instrument line that measures specific, user-chosen sets of peptides (and the proteins they come from) in samples like plasma, serum, CSF, tissue, or cell lysate. It works by first separating peptides with liquid chromatography, then using a hybrid quadrupole plus dual-pressure linear ion trap to select and repeatedly fragment chosen target peptides (a method called PRM/MSn), reading out characteristic fragment signals to confirm identity and measure abundance. What distinguishes this platform is that it isn't tied to a fixed protein list: labs build custom PRM panels (aided by PRM Conductor software) that can scale to hundreds of peptides, run on a Vanquish Neo LC front end, and support quantitation from relative comparisons up to absolute concentrations using stable-isotope-labeled standards.

overview.about: The Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Ascend Tribrid is a high-resolution mass spectrometer that identifies and measures proteins in complex biological samples without a predefined target list. It combines three ion-analysis components: a quadrupole (which selects ions of interest), an Orbitrap (which measures mass with high accuracy), and a linear ion trap (which fragments ions to reveal sequence information). This architecture enables deep discovery of low-abundance proteins and their post-translational modifications like phosphorylation and glycosylation. The instrument is particularly suited to in-depth characterization of protein chemistry in cells, tissues, and body fluids.

overview.about: ENRICH-iST is a sample-preparation chemistry that enriches low-abundance proteins from plasma, serum, and other body fluids before mass spectrometry analysis. It uses non-functionalized paramagnetic microbeads coated with a protein corona to selectively capture and concentrate proteins from high-background matrices, then digests them on the bead surface into peptides. These peptides are identified and quantified by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry, typically on a timsTOF instrument. The platform identifies ~3,800 protein groups per sample and adds 50–100% more protein IDs compared to unprocessed plasma, making it a cost-effective alternative to immunodepletion or nanoparticle enrichment for deep plasma proteomics.

overview.about: ProteomEdge provides targeted mass spectrometry panels for absolute protein quantification, delivered through CRO service partners. Each panel uses heavy-labelled recombinant protein standards so that a known reference is measured alongside every target, giving absolute concentrations. Panels are application-specific: ApoEdge covers about 18 apolipoproteins, ComplemEdge about 81 complement proteins, LiverEdge about 39 liver-disease proteins, and DiscoveryEdge175 about 176 targets. A larger DiscoveryEdge600 panel adds about 620 protein standards backed by more than 6,000 experimentally verified peptides, using the same heavy-labelled absolute-quantification chemistry and extending toward broader discovery-scale work. The company grew out of the Human Protein Atlas program. Independent validation of the panels is not yet established, and a cited AstraZeneca phase-1 trial (of a PCSK9 inhibitor) used an apolipoprotein MS readout, but named-product use is not confirmed.
